evaluations.reason: The lesson accurately describes the three core stages of RAG: retrieving relevant documents from an external source, augmenting the user prompt with the retrieved context, and generating an answer grounded in that context using a language model.
The lesson is accessible to readers with no technical background, using clear, intuitive analogies such as closed-book versus open-book exams and defining baseline terms in plain English.
The lesson includes multiple practical examples, notably an end-to-end walkthrough of a bakery adding a new drink to its menu update file and an employee inquiring about a remote work policy.
Technical concepts including Artificial Intelligence, Language Model, Hallucination, and Knowledge Base are defined clearly at or before the point of introduction without relying on undefined jargon.
The lesson covers all required aspects: definition of RAG, why it is needed, step-by-step mechanics, practical benefits, and real-world limitations such as reliance on source quality and latency.

The progression is logical and structured, starting with an introductory problem statement, explaining core mechanisms conceptually, detailing the technical flow, providing concrete application examples, analyzing tradeoffs, and concluding with a summary.

improvement_summary: No improvements required. The lesson meets all rubric criteria with technically accurate, accessible, and complete explanations.
